sections.name: Ferry spawn and departures
sections.prediction: The five-body ferry spawn separates into a near S1 ascent, a Cooper/S2 approach and the Shore Toe commitment. M03 blocks a direct lower diagonal into S2; Net Street behind it is 4 m deep. W01 may reveal a standing Net player without revealing the bomb or Shore Toe.
sections.follower: A follower can remain below the S1 mouth or shift along Net Street toward S2. Supporting an ascending leader is height-dependent; do not infer a clear trade over the crest wall.
sections.opponent: The W01 observer must approach the sill and turn away from Press. A ground player can challenge the aperture or crouch behind the lower crest; the whole spawn is not assumed visible.

sections.name: Ridge spawn and departures
sections.prediction: CT divides around Bell Building: Inn/upper bridge, School ascent and Bell ascent reach different fronts. M17 prevents a ridge player from treating both descents as one visible launch pad.
sections.follower: The follower can support the Inn-facing lane or join Bell court; the building prevents immediate support across its body. Five spawn centers are 2 m apart.
sections.opponent: A captured upper bridge can challenge the Inn porch. That does not automatically expose the S8 approach behind Bell Building.

sections.name: Laundry to Press territory
sections.prediction: The Press passage is a 4 m clear, 3 m high supported connection, with a straight reciprocal challenge. Going around the occupied Press/Potter fronts reaches S3 or the north side of Press porch instead; those are distinct onward decisions.
sections.follower: F can see along I01 once L passes the west mouth. It cannot support around the northeastern M05 return without taking another position. A failed passage challenge can withdraw toward Laundry.
sections.opponent: O can deny I01 from the porch, but must leave that angle to cover the north Press route or the bridge. M05 is a complete full-height occluder, not low cover.

sections.name: A precinct and two local ascents
sections.prediction: S3 arrives below Chapel and turns into the A approach; S4 reaches the bridge-facing shoulder beside West Homes. M08 blocks the direct diagonal from the bridge stance to both A local ascents. A 6×6 m plant footprint is an authoring assumption.
sections.follower: F at the Chapel edge can follow/trade into A but cannot simultaneously support a teammate at S4 through M08. The cistern rim offers crouch preparation with open side exposure.
sections.opponent: An A anchor can yield north around the cistern, or contest the Chapel approach. Watching Upper Bridge requires a separate position east of M08 and gives up immediate S3 coverage.
captures: A entry / O01 standing and crouching

sections.name: Middle span and Taverna receiving territory
sections.prediction: A 28 m span reaches the western half of I04. O03 blocks the bridge-facing stance from the two district departures; the crossers go south of its tip, then choose Fountain or the north School porch. This is an occupied receiving room with 3 m clear height, not a safe zone.
sections.follower: F0 cannot trade around the return immediately. F1 must advance to (82,54,+4), where the ray to O passes south of the return tip. The 5.55 m gap south of O03 permits two-body movement and a retreat.
sections.opponent: O can hold the east departure or push the room; S can pressure the north doorway. One defender may reposition between them, but the return prevents the same fixed bridge stance from seeing all three fronts. No peeker or utility claim is made.

sections.name: Shore Toe commitment and Lower Harbor bend
sections.prediction: The shore route remains at 0 m and has no middle-ravine escape. The Boat Shed corner and Salt Store form a 6 m-deep lower-harbor bend before B. L can stop before the final corner while F retains the paid return to Shore Toe.
sections.follower: F sees L in the harbor approach but loses immediate site support when L rounds the M10 corner. The retreat is through the same ground route; a middle teammate can relieve it by threatening S5.
sections.opponent: A B defender can push the bend but leaves a site-facing position and must account for the east descents. Salt Store blocks an automatic upper reserve view into the entire harbor; exact S5 grade exposures remain to capture.

sections.name: B precinct, Customs and east descents
sections.prediction: B is bounded by complete Boat Shed, Customs and Waterfront Homes. S5 arrives on the Salt-store side; S6 arrives behind Customs through the L porch. The 6×6 m site is an authoring footprint, not implemented planting behavior.
sections.follower: The shore follower needs to round the same M10 corner to trade the final entry. A teammate through I02 can support the S6 front, but Customs prevents immediate fire support across the whole site.
sections.opponent: O02 hides a crouching body from some ground positions; S5/S6 elevation can reveal behind it. A lone holder must move between shore, S5 and Customs fronts. That is a hypothesis, not proof that all three are independently contestable.
captures: S5 and S6 bottom/mid/top and reverse

sections.name: East middle reserve and ascent choice
sections.prediction: Winning the Taverna north exit reaches a narrow public porch, then either S7 or the School arcade toward S8. Fountain Court instead reaches S5/S6. School and East Homes keep these from becoming one undivided middle pad.
sections.follower: The arcade provides 4 m clear passage and straight support, while F at Taverna cannot fire through School mass. School porch depth is 4 m north of Taverna, sufficient for passing but exposed to a push from either ascent.
sections.opponent: O can defend the arcade east mouth or fall to Bell stepside; it cannot see S7 through School. A CT yielding this reserve territory concedes alternate B pressure as well as upper access.

sections.name: Upper crossing and West Lookout
sections.prediction: The 26 m civic span and 4 m-high Inn arch retain direct long support. West Homes creates an occupied receiving shoulder: north around its end reaches A, south reaches S4 and a lower district. W02 gives limited cross-level information from the span itself.
sections.follower: F can trade along the span, unlike F0 at the Taverna return. After L goes north behind M08, that support ends. The bridge remains an exposed commitment with an ordinary reversible retreat.
sections.opponent: O can challenge the span but cannot simultaneously defend S3 or A through M08. CT pressure from the bridge plus a west-middle survivor on S3 is a real two-front scenario only when that survivor is already west.
captures: West Lookout north retreat and S4 option

sections.name: Bounded Laundry information
sections.prediction: W01 is a 3 m-wide observation aperture: global sill 5.20, head 6.30, panel top 6.60. The selected standing eye ray crosses the wall at z5.461. Crouching eye crosses below the sill; this is a geometric prediction to test.
sections.follower: The support can stay in Laundry, but cannot shoot through the wall beside W01. Approaching the opening is a deliberate exposure; it is not a route or a safe omniscient window.
sections.opponent: The selected ground standing ray is reciprocal and clears the lower crest wall at y34 by about .22 m. Crouching ground exposure and exact body slices need compiled images; do not mistake the eye ray for full-body visibility.
captures: Both crouched eyes and body silhouettes

scenarios.attack: Two T establish Laundry/Press; one stays to keep bridge pressure credible, two can work S3/S4 toward A. Shore presence remains a separate commitment.
scenarios.defense: CT may send an upper-crossing A anchor, lower B anchor and east-middle reserve; actual opening races remain unmeasured.

scenarios.attack: Shore pair stops at Lower Harbor while the middle group earns I04 and chooses S5 pressure. The shore group cannot escape upward inside the ravine.
scenarios.defense: B holder can push the bend or delay a ground entry while reserve chooses between retaining Taverna and descending. Visible bridge pressure is incomplete bomb information.

scenarios.attack: Press player shows span pressure, then withdraws to S4/A or all the way to Shore Toe. This is only credible when the actual remaining time supports the journey.
scenarios.defense: Taverna observer can retain crossing information or leave to reinforce a site, giving up the entry. O03 does not grant both fronts from one fixed stance.

scenarios.attack: One player retaining the bridgehead gives two advancing players a potential return. If that player is lost, upper or shore reconnection is an expensive territorial consequence.
scenarios.defense: Pressure the north bridgehead or middle span rather than automatically adding a new graph edge. Reconnection is contingent, not guaranteed.

scenarios.attack: One player chooses A/Chapel while another elects West Lookout or local-ascent delay; M08 prevents one fixed player covering all of them.
scenarios.defense: Upper crossing plus a survivor ALREADY on west middle can create two fronts. If both CTs are east, the middle-plus-ascent investment must be measured against the clock.

scenarios.attack: One player holds ground; the partner repositions between descent and shore pressure. O02 is conditional crouch cover, not full elevated protection.
scenarios.defense: A survivor already on east middle can choose S5 or S6. A survivor at A must pay R09; the shore route is not advertised as an emergency retake.

captureProtocol: Compile frozen AML later; hash source and active rendered identity. Apply public camera form AFTER compile ready, assert actual #model.dataset.view equals request, then capture. URL-only poses are not accepted. Pair roof-on/cutaway and opposing/follower views. Every stair additionally needs bottom, midpoint and top plus reverse views; every route walked both directions with unchanged body.
